meta.remediation: Restrict access by IP whitelist, VPN, or require multi-factor authentication (MFA).

groupedFindings.title: Administrative Panels Exposure
groupedFindings.remediation: Restrict access by IP whitelist, VPN, or require multi-factor authentication (MFA).

groupedFindings.name: ai & llm exposure

meta.title: AI & LLM Endpoint Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for publicly exposed AI/LLM API routes (e.g., /api/chat, /api/generate, /v1/chat/completions) and vector DB endpoints.
meta.whyItMatters: Unprotected AI endpoints invite costly token theft, denial-of-wallet attacks, and prompt injection exploits.
meta.defaultFix: Enforce strict authentication, user-level rate limiting, and input validation on all AI endpoints.
meta.remediation: Enforce strict authentication, user-level rate limiting, and input validation on all AI endpoints.

groupedFindings.title: AI & LLM Endpoint Exposure
groupedFindings.remediation: Enforce strict authentication, user-level rate limiting, and input validation on all AI endpoints.

apiCommunication.summary: spa_api_client — Clients: Angular HttpClient, Fetch API, GraphQL | 3 same-origin route(s), 1 external origin(s)

meta.title: Client-Side API Communication & Endpoint Discovery
meta.plainExplanation: Inspects Single Page Application (SPA) HTML, JavaScript bundles (Angular, React, Vue, Next.js), runtime configuration files (/assets/config.json, /config.json, /env.js), and CSP connect-src directives to map client-to-API communication, discover backend REST/GraphQL/WebSocket endpoints, and detect unauthenticated API data exposure or insecure API configurations.
meta.whyItMatters: Modern SPAs communicate directly with same-origin or external backend APIs via Angular HttpClient, Fetch, Axios, or GraphQL. Hardcoded development/localhost API URLs, plaintext HTTP API endpoints on HTTPS pages, exposed runtime config files, or unauthenticated JSON API endpoints can leak sensitive customer data, credentials, and internal service topology.
meta.defaultFix: Use environment-specific production builds (e.g., Angular environment.prod.ts without dev proxy.conf.json localhost URLs), enforce HTTPS for all API origins, require authentication on sensitive REST/GraphQL endpoints, remove secrets from public /assets/config.json files, and restrict allowed API origins via Content-Security-Policy connect-src and strict CORS policies.
meta.remediation: Use environment-specific production builds (e.g., Angular environment.prod.ts without dev proxy.conf.json localhost URLs), enforce HTTPS for all API origins, require authentication on sensitive REST/GraphQL endpoints, remove secrets from public /assets/config.json files, and restrict allowed API origins via Content-Security-Policy connect-src and strict CORS policies.

groupedFindings.title: Client-Side API Communication & Endpoint Discovery
groupedFindings.remediation: Use environment-specific production builds (e.g., Angular environment.prod.ts without dev proxy.conf.json localhost URLs), enforce HTTPS for all API origins, require authentication on sensitive REST/GraphQL endpoints, remove secrets from public /assets/config.json files, and restrict allowed API origins via Content-Security-Policy connect-src and strict CORS policies.

meta.remediation: Enforce authentication and role-based access control on all internal endpoints and disable debug routes in production.

groupedFindings.name: clickjacking protection

issues.issue: No X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors — iframe embedding possible

groupedFindings.fix: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' (or SAMEORIGIN) and 'Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors none' (or 'self') headers to prevent unauthorized embedding in iframes.

meta.title: Clickjacking Protection
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if your web pages can be embedded in an iframe on third-party websites.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers can trick users into clicking invisible buttons or submitting forms on your site while thinking they are on another site.
meta.defaultFix: Add the "X-Frame-Options: DENY" or "Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'" HTTP header.
meta.remediation: Add the "X-Frame-Options: DENY" or "Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'" HTTP header.

groupedFindings.title: Clickjacking Protection
groupedFindings.remediation: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' (or SAMEORIGIN) and 'Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors none' (or 'self') headers to prevent unauthorized embedding in iframes.

groupedFindings.name: cookie security

meta.title: Cookie Security Attributes
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies that cookies have Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite flags configured.
meta.whyItMatters: Cookies missing HttpOnly can be stolen via XSS, and cookies missing Secure can be intercepted over unencrypted networks.
meta.defaultFix: Set "Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax" (or SameSite=Strict) on all session and sensitive cookies.
meta.remediation: Set "Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax" (or SameSite=Strict) on all session and sensitive cookies.

groupedFindings.title: Cookie Security Attributes
groupedFindings.remediation: Set "Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax" (or SameSite=Strict) on all session and sensitive cookies.

groupedFindings.name: cors misconfiguration

meta.title: CORS Configuration
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for overly permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policies like wildcard origins with credentials.
meta.whyItMatters: Permissive CORS allows malicious third-party websites to read sensitive user data from your API via cross-origin requests.
meta.defaultFix: Specify explicit trusted origins in the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" header and avoid reflecting arbitrary origins with credentials.
meta.remediation: Specify explicit trusted origins in the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" header and avoid reflecting arbitrary origins with credentials.

groupedFindings.title: CORS Configuration
groupedFindings.remediation: Specify explicit trusted origins in the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" header and avoid reflecting arbitrary origins with credentials.

groupedFindings.name: directory listing

meta.title: Directory Indexing / Listing
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if web server directories without index files display automatic file listings.
meta.whyItMatters: Allows attackers to browse internal folder contents, discover forgotten backups, uploaded files, and source code.
meta.defaultFix: Disable directory browsing in web server configuration (e.g., "Options -Indexes" in Apache, "autoindex off" in Nginx).
meta.remediation: Disable directory browsing in web server configuration (e.g., "Options -Indexes" in Apache, "autoindex off" in Nginx).

groupedFindings.title: Directory Indexing / Listing
groupedFindings.remediation: Disable directory browsing in web server configuration (e.g., "Options -Indexes" in Apache, "autoindex off" in Nginx).

groupedFindings.name: env file exposure

meta.title: Environment File Exposure (.env)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if environment configuration files (.env, .env.backup, etc.) are downloadable from the web.
meta.whyItMatters: .env files usually contain database passwords, API secrets, JWT keys, and payment gateway tokens.
meta.defaultFix: Block web server access to all dotfiles (e.g. location ~ /\. { deny all; }) and store sensitive configs outside web roots.
meta.remediation: Block web server access to all dotfiles (e.g. location ~ /\. { deny all; }) and store sensitive configs outside web roots.

groupedFindings.title: Environment File Exposure (.env)
groupedFindings.remediation: Block web server access to all dotfiles (e.g. location ~ /\. { deny all; }) and store sensitive configs outside web roots.

groupedFindings.name: frontend security

meta.title: Frontend Source Maps & Dev Artifacts
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed production JavaScript source maps (.js.map), debug modes, and hardcoded API tokens.
meta.whyItMatters: Source maps reconstruct original client-side source code, revealing internal endpoints, comments, and architectural flaws.
meta.defaultFix: Do not deploy .map files to public production servers; generate source maps only for internal error tracking.
meta.remediation: Do not deploy .map files to public production servers; generate source maps only for internal error tracking.

groupedFindings.title: Frontend Source Maps & Dev Artifacts
groupedFindings.remediation: Do not deploy .map files to public production servers; generate source maps only for internal error tracking.

groupedFindings.name: .git exposure

meta.title: Git Repository Exposure (.git)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if the .git folder or .git/HEAD is publicly accessible on the web server.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed Git folders allow attackers to download your entire source code repository, history, and embedded secrets.
meta.defaultFix: Configure your web server to strictly block access to the .git directory or exclude .git during deployment.
meta.remediation: Configure your web server to strictly block access to the .git directory or exclude .git during deployment.

groupedFindings.title: Git Repository Exposure (.git)
groupedFindings.remediation: Configure your web server to strictly block access to the .git directory or exclude .git during deployment.

groupedFindings.name: graphql introspection

meta.title: GraphQL Introspection & Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if GraphQL schema introspection is enabled in production environments.
meta.whyItMatters: Introspection exposes your entire GraphQL schema, types, queries, and mutations to any unauthenticated caller.
meta.defaultFix: Disable GraphQL schema introspection in production deployments.
meta.remediation: Disable GraphQL schema introspection in production deployments.

groupedFindings.title: GraphQL Introspection & Security
groupedFindings.remediation: Disable GraphQL schema introspection in production deployments.

groupedFindings.name: http methods

meta.title: Dangerous HTTP Methods
meta.plainExplanation: Tests whether dangerous or unnecessary HTTP verbs (PUT, DELETE, TRACE, OPTIONS) are accepted.
meta.whyItMatters: TRACE enables Cross-Site Tracing (XST) attacks; improperly configured PUT/DELETE allows unauthorized file modification.
meta.defaultFix: Disable TRACE and restrict HTTP methods to only GET, POST, and HEAD for public web pages.
meta.remediation: Disable TRACE and restrict HTTP methods to only GET, POST, and HEAD for public web pages.

groupedFindings.title: Dangerous HTTP Methods
groupedFindings.remediation: Disable TRACE and restrict HTTP methods to only GET, POST, and HEAD for public web pages.

groupedFindings.name: https redirect
groupedFindings.detail: Target is already HTTP — HTTPS check skipped

meta.title: HTTP to HTTPS Redirection
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies that unencrypted HTTP connections are automatically redirected to secure HTTPS.
meta.whyItMatters: Unencrypted HTTP traffic can be intercepted, read, or modified by attackers on public networks.
meta.defaultFix: Configure a permanent (301) redirect from HTTP to HTTPS across all web server hosts.
meta.remediation: Configure a permanent (301) redirect from HTTP to HTTPS across all web server hosts.

groupedFindings.title: HTTP to HTTPS Redirection
groupedFindings.remediation: Configure a permanent (301) redirect from HTTP to HTTPS across all web server hosts.

groupedFindings.name: jwt security
groupedFindings.detail: No JWT tokens found in probed endpoints

meta.title: JSON Web Token (JWT) Security
meta.plainExplanation: Audits JWT implementations for "none" algorithm flaws, weak secret keys, and exposed token endpoints.
meta.whyItMatters: Vulnerable JWT implementations allow attackers to forge tokens and impersonate administrators.
meta.defaultFix: Use strong cryptographic algorithms (RS256 or high-entropy HS256) and strictly reject tokens with "alg": "none".
meta.remediation: Use strong cryptographic algorithms (RS256 or high-entropy HS256) and strictly reject tokens with "alg": "none".

groupedFindings.title: JSON Web Token (JWT) Security
groupedFindings.remediation: Use strong cryptographic algorithms (RS256 or high-entropy HS256) and strictly reject tokens with "alg": "none".

groupedFindings.name: open redirect

meta.title: Open Redirect Vulnerability
meta.plainExplanation: Tests if redirect parameters (e.g. ?url=, ?redirect=) accept arbitrary external websites.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers craft believable phishing links using your trusted domain that redirect victims to malicious sites.
meta.defaultFix: Validate target URLs against a strict whitelist of internal relative paths or approved domains.
meta.remediation: Validate target URLs against a strict whitelist of internal relative paths or approved domains.

groupedFindings.title: Open Redirect Vulnerability
groupedFindings.remediation: Validate target URLs against a strict whitelist of internal relative paths or approved domains.

groupedFindings.name: rate limiting
groupedFindings.detail: 15/15 burst requests succeeded — no rate limiting detected (brute-force risk)
groupedFindings.fix: Implement rate limiting at the application level (e.g., Laravel's ThrottleRequests) or web server level (e.g., Nginx 'limit_req') to protect against brute-force and DoS attacks.

meta.title: Rate Limiting & Abuse Prevention
meta.plainExplanation: Tests whether rapid bursts of requests trigger HTTP 429 Too Many Requests or rate-limit headers.
meta.whyItMatters: Endpoints without rate limiting are vulnerable to denial of service, credential stuffing, and scraping.
meta.defaultFix: Implement rate limiting at the reverse proxy (e.g. Nginx limit_req) or application layer.
meta.remediation: Implement rate limiting at the reverse proxy (e.g. Nginx limit_req) or application layer.

groupedFindings.title: Rate Limiting & Abuse Prevention
groupedFindings.remediation: Implement rate limiting at the application level (e.g., Laravel's ThrottleRequests) or web server level (e.g., Nginx 'limit_req') to protect against brute-force and DoS attacks.

groupedFindings.name: robots.txt disclosure

meta.title: Robots.txt & Sitemap Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Analyzes robots.txt and sitemap.xml for disallow rules pointing to sensitive hidden directories.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers read robots.txt to discover hidden admin panels, staging areas, and private endpoints.
meta.defaultFix: Do not rely on robots.txt for security; enforce authentication on all sensitive endpoints.
meta.remediation: Do not rely on robots.txt for security; enforce authentication on all sensitive endpoints.

groupedFindings.title: Robots.txt & Sitemap Disclosure
groupedFindings.remediation: Do not rely on robots.txt for security; enforce authentication on all sensitive endpoints.

groupedFindings.name: security headers
groupedFindings.fix: Implement the missing security headers in your web server configuration (e.g., in Nginx 'add_header' or Apache 'Header set') to protect against XSS, clickjacking, and mime-type sniffing.

meta.title: HTTP Security Headers
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for critical defensive headers: HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, CSP, etc.
meta.whyItMatters: Missing security headers leaves users exposed to clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and cross-site scripting.
meta.defaultFix: Configure your web server to supply HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and Referrer-Policy headers.
meta.remediation: Configure your web server to supply HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and Referrer-Policy headers.

groupedFindings.title: HTTP Security Headers
groupedFindings.remediation: Implement the missing security headers in your web server configuration (e.g., in Nginx 'add_header' or Apache 'Header set') to protect against XSS, clickjacking, and mime-type sniffing.

groupedFindings.name: sensitive files

meta.title: Sensitive Files & Configurations
meta.plainExplanation: Scans for exposed database dumps, configuration backups, credentials, and docker-compose files.
meta.whyItMatters: Leaked configuration and database dump files grant instant access to sensitive databases.
meta.defaultFix: Store backups, SQL dumps, and configuration files outside the web root directory.
meta.remediation: Store backups, SQL dumps, and configuration files outside the web root directory.

groupedFindings.name: server version disclosure

meta.title: Server Software Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if Server header reveals software names and exact version numbers (e.g., Apache/2.4.41).
meta.whyItMatters: Detailed version information allows attackers to look up specific CVE exploits for that exact version.
meta.defaultFix: Set ServerTokens Prod in Apache or server_tokens off in Nginx.
meta.remediation: Set ServerTokens Prod in Apache or server_tokens off in Nginx.

groupedFindings.title: Server Software Disclosure
groupedFindings.remediation: Set ServerTokens Prod in Apache or server_tokens off in Nginx.

groupedFindings.name: sql error disclosure

meta.title: Database Error Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Tests if query strings trigger verbose database error messages (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, MSSQL).
meta.whyItMatters: Database error messages reveal schema structures and confirm the presence of SQL injection vulnerabilities.
meta.defaultFix: Disable detailed database error output in production and use generic error messages.
meta.remediation: Disable detailed database error output in production and use generic error messages.

groupedFindings.title: Database Error Disclosure
groupedFindings.remediation: Disable detailed database error output in production and use generic error messages.

groupedFindings.name: sql injection

meta.title: SQL Injection (SQLi)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests input fields and parameters for SQL syntax manipulation and time-based delays.
meta.whyItMatters: SQL injection allows attackers to bypass authentication, read, modify, or delete the entire database.
meta.defaultFix: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for all database interactions; avoid string concatenation.
meta.remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for all database interactions; avoid string concatenation.

groupedFindings.title: SQL Injection (SQLi)
groupedFindings.remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for all database interactions; avoid string concatenation.

groupedFindings.name: supply chain & sri

meta.title: Supply Chain & Subresource Integrity (SRI)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks whether external CDN scripts and stylesheets utilize Subresource Integrity (integrity and crossorigin attributes).
meta.whyItMatters: If a third-party CDN is compromised, scripts without SRI hashes can inject malicious code directly into your visitors' browsers.
meta.defaultFix: Include cryptographic integrity hashes (e.g., integrity="sha384-...") on all external script and link tags.
meta.remediation: Include cryptographic integrity hashes (e.g., integrity="sha384-...") on all external script and link tags.

groupedFindings.title: Supply Chain & Subresource Integrity (SRI)
groupedFindings.remediation: Include cryptographic integrity hashes (e.g., integrity="sha384-...") on all external script and link tags.

groupedFindings.name: ssl/tls check
groupedFindings.detail: Server not using HTTPS at all
groupedFindings.fix: Enable HTTPS (TLS) immediately to encrypt all data in transit. You can use Let's Encrypt for a free, trusted certificate.

meta.title: SSL / TLS Certificate & Encryption
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies SSL certificate validity, expiration, hostname matching, and secure TLS protocol versions.
meta.whyItMatters: Expired or untrusted certificates cause browser warnings and leave traffic vulnerable to interception.
meta.defaultFix: Renew your SSL certificate, enable auto-renewal via Let's Encrypt, and disable obsolete TLS 1.0/1.1.
meta.remediation: Renew your SSL certificate, enable auto-renewal via Let's Encrypt, and disable obsolete TLS 1.0/1.1.

groupedFindings.title: SSL / TLS Certificate & Encryption
groupedFindings.remediation: Enable HTTPS (TLS) immediately to encrypt all data in transit. You can use Let's Encrypt for a free, trusted certificate.

findings.name: cookie security

meta.title: Cookie Security Attributes
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies that cookies have Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite flags configured.
meta.whyItMatters: Cookies missing HttpOnly can be stolen via XSS, and cookies missing Secure can be intercepted over unencrypted networks.
meta.defaultFix: Set "Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax" (or SameSite=Strict) on all session and sensitive cookies.
meta.remediation: Set "Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax" (or SameSite=Strict) on all session and sensitive cookies.

findings.title: Cookie Security Attributes
findings.remediation: Set "Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax" (or SameSite=Strict) on all session and sensitive cookies.

findings.name: cors misconfiguration

meta.title: CORS Configuration
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for overly permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policies like wildcard origins with credentials.
meta.whyItMatters: Permissive CORS allows malicious third-party websites to read sensitive user data from your API via cross-origin requests.
meta.defaultFix: Specify explicit trusted origins in the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" header and avoid reflecting arbitrary origins with credentials.
meta.remediation: Specify explicit trusted origins in the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" header and avoid reflecting arbitrary origins with credentials.

findings.title: CORS Configuration
findings.remediation: Specify explicit trusted origins in the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" header and avoid reflecting arbitrary origins with credentials.

findings.name: directory listing

meta.title: Directory Indexing / Listing
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if web server directories without index files display automatic file listings.
meta.whyItMatters: Allows attackers to browse internal folder contents, discover forgotten backups, uploaded files, and source code.
meta.defaultFix: Disable directory browsing in web server configuration (e.g., "Options -Indexes" in Apache, "autoindex off" in Nginx).
meta.remediation: Disable directory browsing in web server configuration (e.g., "Options -Indexes" in Apache, "autoindex off" in Nginx).

findings.title: Directory Indexing / Listing
findings.remediation: Disable directory browsing in web server configuration (e.g., "Options -Indexes" in Apache, "autoindex off" in Nginx).

findings.name: env file exposure

meta.title: Environment File Exposure (.env)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if environment configuration files (.env, .env.backup, etc.) are downloadable from the web.
meta.whyItMatters: .env files usually contain database passwords, API secrets, JWT keys, and payment gateway tokens.
meta.defaultFix: Block web server access to all dotfiles (e.g. location ~ /\. { deny all; }) and store sensitive configs outside web roots.
meta.remediation: Block web server access to all dotfiles (e.g. location ~ /\. { deny all; }) and store sensitive configs outside web roots.

findings.title: Environment File Exposure (.env)
findings.remediation: Block web server access to all dotfiles (e.g. location ~ /\. { deny all; }) and store sensitive configs outside web roots.

findings.name: frontend security

meta.title: Frontend Source Maps & Dev Artifacts
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed production JavaScript source maps (.js.map), debug modes, and hardcoded API tokens.
meta.whyItMatters: Source maps reconstruct original client-side source code, revealing internal endpoints, comments, and architectural flaws.
meta.defaultFix: Do not deploy .map files to public production servers; generate source maps only for internal error tracking.
meta.remediation: Do not deploy .map files to public production servers; generate source maps only for internal error tracking.

findings.title: Frontend Source Maps & Dev Artifacts
findings.remediation: Do not deploy .map files to public production servers; generate source maps only for internal error tracking.

findings.name: .git exposure

meta.defaultFix: Configure your web server to strictly block access to the .git directory or exclude .git during deployment.
meta.remediation: Configure your web server to strictly block access to the .git directory or exclude .git during deployment.

findings.title: Git Repository Exposure (.git)

meta.remediation: Disable GraphQL schema introspection in production deployments.

findings.title: GraphQL Introspection & Security
findings.remediation: Disable GraphQL schema introspection in production deployments.

meta.defaultFix: Disable TRACE and restrict HTTP methods to only GET, POST, and HEAD for public web pages.
meta.remediation: Disable TRACE and restrict HTTP methods to only GET, POST, and HEAD for public web pages.

findings.title: Dangerous HTTP Methods
findings.remediation: Disable TRACE and restrict HTTP methods to only GET, POST, and HEAD for public web pages.

meta.remediation: Configure a permanent (301) redirect from HTTP to HTTPS across all web server hosts.

meta.remediation: Use strong cryptographic algorithms (RS256 or high-entropy HS256) and strictly reject tokens with "alg": "none".

meta.defaultFix: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for all database interactions; avoid string concatenation.
meta.remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for all database interactions; avoid string concatenation.

meta.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests if user inputs in query parameters are reflected unsanitized in the HTML page body.
meta.whyItMatters: XSS allows attackers to execute malicious JavaScript in victims' browsers, stealing cookies and session tokens.
meta.defaultFix: Sanitize and HTML-encode all user input before outputting it into web pages, and deploy a strong CSP.
meta.remediation: Sanitize and HTML-encode all user input before outputting it into web pages, and deploy a strong CSP.
